item.title: Who Approves Trump’s Washington Makeover Projects?
item.description: The Supreme Court gave a green light to the new White House ballroom, but several of the president’s other Washington projects remain stalled.
item.dc:creator: David A. Fahrenthold, Luke Broadwater, Zach Montague, Junho Lee and Elena Shao
item.category: White House East Wing and Ballroom (Washington, DC)
Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:description: The Supreme Court ruled on Monday that President Trump could continue his construction of a huge new ballroom for the White House where the East Wing used to be.

item.title: Deaths of 2 Men in Los Angeles Police Custody Set Off Investigations
item.description: Mayor Karen Bass questioned police training to handle mental health crises after the city released graphic video footage of officers’ actions.
item.dc:creator: Jill Cowan and Shawn Hubler

item.title: Billionaires Sent Montana Prices Soaring. Can Democrats Capitalize?
item.description: For years, Democrats have failed to harness the anger of Montanans contending with out-of-state wealth driving up costs. This year, a smokejumper thinks he can succeed.
item.dc:creator: Jack Healy
item.media:credit: Will Warasila for The New York Times
item.media:description: Sam Forstag, a telegenic firefighter and union leader, is the Democratic candidate for a House race in Montana.

item.title: The Navy’s Logistical Nightmare in the Iran War
item.description: Amid a crew morale crisis, the military has replaced the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East with another aircraft carrier. Our Pentagon reporter John Ismay, a Navy veteran, explains how the challenges to supply ships in the area will most likely remain the same.
item.dc:creator: John Ismay, Gilad Thaler, Simon Ducroquet, Stephanie Swart, Joey Sendaydiego and Pierre Kattar

item.title: Six Takeaways From the Massachusetts Primaries
item.description: Senator Ed Markey, 80, trounced a younger challenger who had made an argument for generational change. Two other longtime Democratic lawmakers hung on, too.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:description: Senator Ed Markey, who has served in Washington for 50 years, easily beat back a challenge from a younger Democrat.

item.title: Longtime Democratic Congressman Defeats Progressive Rival in Massachusetts
item.description: Representative Stephen Lynch, 71, a centrist, beat Patrick Roath, 39, in a primary that reflected the party’s generational and ideological divides.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross/The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Stephen Lynch’s victory puts him in a strong position to win another term representing Massachusetts’s Eighth Congressional District.

item.title: Officials in Mississippi City Fire Police Chief Over Racist Texts
item.description: Mississippi Today, Verite News and The Times had revealed the chief’s texts as his officers were under scrutiny for the fatal shooting of a Black toddler.
item.dc:creator: Mukta Joshi and Joseph Cranney
item.media:description: Police Chief Harold Vanderford was fired by city leaders after routinely using degrading language and racist slurs against Black people in his text messages.

item.title: Former Biden White House Aide Wins Massachusetts Democratic House Primary
item.description: Dan Koh, who ran with the endorsement of former President Joseph R. Biden Jr., topped a crowded field to secure the nomination in the safely Democratic Sixth Congressional District.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Dan Koh is one of just two congressional candidates who were endorsed by former President Joseph R. Biden Jr.

item.title: A Plan to Eradicate the Deer on Catalina Island Will Proceed, Organizers Say
item.description: After a judge issued a tentative ruling on a legal challenge Tuesday, the Catalina Island Conservancy said that it would begin the first phase of its plan to kill nearly all of the 2,000 deer on the California island.
item.dc:creator: Soumya Karlamangla and Tim Arango
item.media:credit: Sinna Nasseri for The New York Times
item.media:description: Deer on Catalina Island in 2023.

item.title: Trump to Nominate Hung Cao as Navy Secretary
item.description: The announcement came amid a purge of leadership at the Pentagon and a stalling war effort against Iran.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: The acting Navy secretary, Hung Cao, is considered more aligned with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth than his predecessor was.

item.title: Mike Minogue Wins G.O.P. Nomination for Massachusetts Governor
item.description: Mr. Minogue, who for years ran a medical device company, will face Gov. Maura Healey, a Democrat seeking a second term, in the November election.
item.dc:creator: Jenna Russell
item.media:credit: Pat Greenhouse/The Boston Globe, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Republican candidate for governor Mike Minogue in May.

item.title: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey Wins Democratic Nomination
item.description: Maura Healey, a former state attorney general seeking a second term, has been an outspoken critic of President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Jenna Russell
item.media:credit: Kylie Cooper for The New York Times
item.media:description: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey in 2025.

item.title: Ed Markey Wins Massachusetts Democratic Senate Primary, Defeating Younger Challenger
item.description: The oldest senator in Massachusetts history used a progressive message to beat Representative Seth Moulton, 47, defying calls for generational change.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Mel Musto for The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Edward J. Markey ran on a fiercely progressive platform.

item.title: Couple in Florida Kept 4 Children Inside Truck for Years, Prosecutors Say
item.description: Two boys and two girls were kept in a semi truck cab for six years, the authorities said, and the two girls, both under 11 years old, were repeatedly sexually abused.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai
item.media:description: “This was a prison, a rolling prison,” Attorney General James Uthmeier of Florida said on Tuesday.

item.title: Judge Lets Case Against Tyler Robinson, Charlie Kirk Shooting Suspect, Go to Trial
item.description: The judge said prosecutors had presented enough evidence to try the man accused of killing the conservative activist last year, who pleaded not guilty.
item.dc:creator: Jack Healy and Nicholas Bogel-Burroughs
item.media:description: Judge Tony Graf at a preliminary hearing in July for Tyler Robinson, who is accused of fatally shooting Charlie Kirk, in Provo, Utah.

item.title: Federal Judge Dismisses Lawsuit Against Lizzo and Her Touring Company
item.description: The singer, who has faced several lawsuits asserting harassment, discrimination and a hostile work environment, has repeatedly denied wrongdoing.
item.dc:creator: Alena Cerro
item.media:description: The case dismissed on Tuesday was filed regarding Lizzo’s 2023 tour.

item.title: Joint Chiefs Chairman Says Military Has ‘No Plans’ to Send Troops to the Polls
item.description: Gen. Dan Caine, President Trump’s top military adviser, appeared to renounce the possibility of the military interfering in the 2026 midterms.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Anna Rose Layden for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gen. Dan Caine, President Trump’s top military adviser. appeared to renounce the possibility that the military would interfere with the vote in an Aug. 28 letter to Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan.

item.title: Justice Department Sues Kansas City Schools Over Gender Policy
item.description: In the first such lawsuit, the Trump administration accused the district of hiding students’ gender transition from their parents against federal law.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender
item.media:description: The federal government has sued a public school district over gender identity and laws that ensure parents have access to their children’s records.

item.title: A Nearly 200-Year-Old Museum Known for Its T. Rex Faces Extinction
item.description: The Academy of Natural Sciences in Philadelphia, which is affiliated with Drexel University, cited attendance struggles and higher costs in its decision to close.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.media:description: The Academy of Natural Sciences in Philadelphia opened in 1828 and is known for its Dinosaur Hall.

item.title: Former President Joe Biden Will Attend Sept. 11 Ceremony in New York
item.description: Mr. Biden will join three other living presidents at the event. President Trump has decided to skip the ceremony and is expected to appear at the Pentagon on the 25th anniversary of the attacks.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman and Dana Rubinstein
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times
item.media:description: Former President Joseph R. Biden Jr. and the former first lady Jill Biden will attend a ceremony in New York commemorating the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks.

item.title: House Censures Republican Accused of Sexually Harassing Two Aides
item.description: Representative Chuck Edwards received a formal rebuke on the floor after a speech in which he apologized for his conduct but said it did not constitute harassment.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:description: Representative Chuck Edwards, Republican of North Carolina, announced last month that he would not seek re-election after the House Ethics Committee recommended that he be reprimanded for his behavior.

item.title: Shooting at Tucson Gay Bar That Killed 2 Investigated as Hate Crime
item.description: Two men were fatally shot in the bar’s parking lot early Monday morning. The suspected gunman, who also died, was carrying a list of other L.G.B.T.Q.-friendly businesses, the police said.
item.dc:creator: Pooja Salhotra and Sheryl Kornman
item.media:description: A growing memorial outside the bar Venture-N in Tucson, Ariz., on Tuesday.

item.title: Haitian Student, Despondent Over Ankle Monitor, Dies in Apparent Suicide
item.description: The 20-year-old was fitted with a tracking device under a Trump administrative initiative targeting Haitians in Springfield, Ohio.
item.dc:creator: Miriam Jordan
item.media:credit: Maddie McGarvey for The New York Times
item.media:description: Friends of Pierre Damas Bel and advocates with the Haitian Community Network in Springfield, Ohio, held a news conference on Tuesday addressing his death.

item.title: Hegseth Targets 7 More Officers as His Frustrated Army Secretary Quits
item.description: The defense secretary’s cuts, which have hit about 10 percent of the military’s top officers, are dividing the Pentagon, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Greg Jaffe, Helene Cooper and Eric Schmitt
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth laid out his vision for the cuts in a speech at Quantico attended by all of the military’s generals and admirals last September.

item.title: Have You Felt Any Impact From Trump’s ‘Big Beautiful Bill’? Tell Us How.
item.description: To help us report upcoming stories, we want to hear whether President Trump’s signature domestic legislation has had any effect on your household budget.
item.dc:creator: Audra D. S. Burch
item.media:description: Major cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) under President Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act are expected to leave people at risk of losing food assistance.

item.title: On Trump’s Ballroom, Chief Justice Finds Himself in an Unusual Spot: In Dissent
item.description: Chief Justice John G. Roberts Jr. has been in the majority in divided cases more times than any other chief since 1953. But not this time.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow
item.category: White House East Wing and Ballroom (Washington, DC)
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross/The New York Times
item.media:description: In his understated way, Chief Justice John G. Roberts Jr. suggested that he was distressed by what the president was doing to the White House.

item.title: Officer Charged in Shooting of College Athlete Who Knocked at Wrong Door
item.description: Prosecutors said the police officer from Upper Pottsgrove, Pa., committed manslaughter when he fired on the student, who was returning from a night out at bars. A homeowner had reported a burglary in progress.
item.dc:creator: Pooja Salhotra
item.media:description: An officer with the Upper Pottsgrove Township Police Department shouted, “Hands up, hands up now, drop to the ground!” at the student. And then he fired.

item.title: Jerome Smith, Freedom Rider Who Challenged Robert Kennedy, Dies at 87
item.description: He castigated Robert F. Kennedy for failing to protect civil rights activists, forcing the attorney general to reckon with the depth of Black anger.
item.dc:creator: Penelope Green
item.media:description: Jerome Smith, left, with Ed Blankenheim, another civil rights activist and Freedom Rider.

item.title: House Votes to Avert Government Shutdown Before Midterm Elections
item.description: Lawmakers sent the legislation to President Trump in an overwhelming vote, reflecting bipartisan enthusiasm around punting a messy spending fight until after the midterms.
item.dc:creator: Catie Edmondson
item.media:description: Speaker Mike Johnson at the Capitol on Tuesday morning. The stopgap bill would keep federal funding flowing at current levels through Dec. 11.

item.title: U.S. Strikes Iran Over Strait of Hormuz Mines, Trump Says
item.description: Iranian officials said the strikes caused significant damage, including killing four people and injuring several dozens at a wedding. Iran said it retaliated by firing on U.S. bases in the region.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Baskar, Farnaz Fassihi and Erica L. Green
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, on Monday.

item.title: Map Apps Are Handling Trump’s Renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America Differently
item.description: Navigation companies face a new dilemma after President Trump ordered Lake Ontario to be renamed Lake America.
item.dc:creator: Victor Mather
item.media:credit: Keito Newman/The Canadian Press, via Associated Press
item.media:description: The companies making map apps are having to respond to President Trump’s order to change the lake’s name from Lake Ontario to Lake America.
